headline: Money got expensive the same week AI needs more of it than ever
dek: The 10-year Treasury yield hit about 5.15% and markets fully price a December Fed hike. In the same week, Anthropic is reportedly set to raise up to $90.4B, and capital cost, not demand, is becoming the limit on growth for crypto, AI infrastructure and energy projects.

asks.text: how we update late-stage AI marks and secondary bids once Anthropic prices; pick comparison companies before Nov 19
portfolio runway with the 10-year above 5% and a December hike, especially AI infrastructure and energy companies that rely on debt
where stablecoin rails still beat card networks in agent payments (business-to-business, cross-border, machine-to-machine)
the size of the PJM ride-through retrofit market (about 10 GW with one year to comply) and re-underwrite robot-AI model companies at CoRL

sections.name: AI Systems
sections.thesis: Frontier AI gets a public price as its compute supplier faces leadership and export-control risk.

items.title: Anthropic IPO reportedly prices Nov 18 and trades Nov 19 as "ANT"
items.why: it would set the first public price for a frontier AI lab, resetting private marks and secondary prices; the reported raise is up to $90.4B (IPO plus private placement) at a $1.4T target, with the book about 6x oversubscribed.
items.watch: final price against the range, first-day trade, and the effect on late-stage AI rounds
items.source_note: Timing and order book come from a single secondhand report; the S-1 (Oct 26) is confirmed. Conflict disclosure: the brief's research editor is Claude, made by Anthropic, so this item reports outside sources only.

items.title: Congress summons Nvidia's Huang over China chip exports; Nvidia reports earnings Nov 17 under an interim CEO
items.why: the main AI compute supplier has a temporary leader (CFO Colette Kress, after Huang's Nov 12 resignation) and faces hearing-driven export enforcement, which adds supply and pricing risk to compute plans.
items.watch: Q3 FY27 earnings Nov 17, the CEO search, and hearings Dec 1–3
items.source_note: Resignation is pre-window (Nov 12); reasons for the exit are unconfirmed and excluded.

items.title: LangChain raises $300M Series C at a $3B valuation, led by CapitalG
items.why: investors are paying up for model-agnostic agent tooling, which cuts against fears that the labs will absorb the tooling layer.
items.watch: whether other agent-tooling rounds price similarly
items.source_note: Funding confirmed; the 7,000 LangSmith customer count is LangChain's own figure.

also_noted: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents complete purchases with user approval each time; see Crypto.
Nebius's CEO reportedly said bond markets are effectively closed to neo-cloud GPU-rental companies (secondhand newsletter).
FAA's Nov 13 nationwide ground stop came days after its AI routing tool SMART went nationwide; no link is confirmed and the vendor denies a role (AI aggregator).
Pre-window: four nonprofits sued Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceX on Nov 12 seeking to freeze new model training (aggregator).

sections.name: Energy & Grid
sections.thesis: Grid access for data centers now comes with performance rules and local politics.

items.title: PJM asks FERC to require data centers of 50 MW or more to ride through grid disturbances
items.why: it creates a retrofit market for power electronics, UPS controls, batteries and stabilizing equipment across about 10 GW of existing loads, after 3.9 GW suddenly dropped off the grid on July 22.
items.watch: FERC comment deadlines, PJM's coming ramp-rate rules, and copycat grid operators

items.title: Voters limited or blocked data centers in 40 of 41 local ballot measures
items.why: community approval is becoming a bottleneck alongside grid capacity, which favors on-site generation and smaller distributed sites.
items.watch: more local moratoria and permitting fights
items.source_note: Single source for the ballot figure.

also_noted: IREN's commercial chief says data center lead times now exceed 7 years in most places (secondhand).
Pre-window: Belgium and ENGIE pushed the deadline for a possible state takeover of the nuclear fleet to Dec 12.

sections.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
sections.thesis: Card networks took consumer agent checkout while exchanges lean on recurring revenue.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet on Amex, Chase, Mastercard and Visa, with no crypto or stablecoins
items.why: the largest consumer agent platform chose card rails for its first agent payments, weakening the thesis that agent commerce defaults to crypto.
items.watch: whether stablecoins get added, and crypto openings in business or machine-to-machine payments
items.source_note: Launch from OpenAI; the no-crypto detail comes from secondary outlets.

items.title: Kraken parent Payward's Q3 adjusted EBITDA falls 67% to $60M as trading volume drops 30%
items.why: client-balance and subscription income rose to 52% of the total, which shows exchanges shifting to recurring revenue and changes how to value them.
items.watch: Q4 volumes in the selloff and the timing of the prediction-markets launch

items.title: BitGo says Unocoin's disputed transfers were signed with Unocoin's own keys
items.why: it shows that in shared-key custody, a custodian's freeze doesn't bind a client that holds enough keys.
items.watch: Unocoin's loss figure and service restart
items.source_note: Single secondhand source; company statements only.

also_noted: BTC fell to about $62,000 on Nov 15, about 23% below its Nov 4 high; US spot BTC ETFs lost $1.91B over seven straight sessions.
New York issued advertising standards for licensed crypto firms; the prediction-market state–federal fight spread to Arkansas (weekly roundup).
Pre-window: the UK House of Lords approved stablecoin perimeter amendments Nov 11; they are not yet law.
Pre-window: Taiwan's draft stablecoin rules restrict issuance mainly to banks; 40-day comment period from Nov 3.

sections.name: Robotics & Autonomy
sections.thesis: General models may absorb robot AI, pushing value toward hardware, data and deployment.

items.title: OpenAI disbands its standalone robotics team, saying its general models now control robots
items.why: if frontier models can run robots, the case for separate robot-AI model startups weakens.
items.watch: CoRL this week and robot-AI startup fundraising
items.source_note: Reorganization confirmed by OpenAI; performance claims are OpenAI's own.

items.title: Pony.ai and Toyota launch fully driverless paid robotaxi service in Guangzhou
items.why: a major carmaker's mass-produced vehicle is now in driverless commercial service, a step toward scale robotaxi manufacturing.
items.watch: fleet size and expansion beyond Guangzhou

also_noted: Pre-window: Tesla says Robotaxi now runs 24/7 in every city it serves (Nov 11).
Coverage gap: no dedicated humanoid funding search this window.

sections.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences
sections.thesis: Pharma M&A exits stay open despite the rate shock.

items.title: J&J to acquire Ollin Biosciences for $2.2B upfront plus up to $1.1B in milestones
items.why: pharma is still paying billions upfront for clinical-stage biotech, so the exit path for private biotech remains open.
items.watch: antitrust timing and Ollin's lead eye-disease programs

also_noted: Novo's CagriSema showed about 21% weight loss vs 2% on placebo at 68 weeks in REDEFINE 9 (secondary source; check the Lancet paper).
Helus Pharma reports positive Phase 3 topline results for HLP003 as an add-on depression treatment (company claim; NDA timeline needs checking).
FDA approved Biocon's Perjeta biosimilar, but US launch is blocked until Q3 2028 at the earliest.
Pre-window, unconfirmed: PharmTech reports signs the FDA shelved its National Priority Voucher pilot; there is no FDA statement.

sections.name: Deep Tech
sections.thesis: Near-term quantum value runs through hybrid quantum–classical systems.

items.title: IBM claims its Nighthawk r2 runs up to 100,000 samples per second, 25x Heron, at SC26
items.why: quantum value is arriving through hybrid systems inside supercomputing centers, which favors scheduling and integration software.
items.watch: the Gordon Bell result for the Cleveland Clinic/RIKEN/IBM protein simulation
items.source_note: Company claims; the IBM/NVIDIA/Fermilab platform was seen only via aggregator.

also_noted: MediaTek raised its 2026 custom AI chip revenue outlook from $2.0B to $2.5B (secondhand).
AMD's MEXT memory engine reportedly halves DRAM requirements (Tom's Hardware).
Unconfirmed: TSMC reportedly approved up to $1B of investment split between OpenAI and Anthropic shares (aggregator only; date unclear).

filtered_out: Filtered out: price and liquidation recaps, CZ's IPO-selloff speculation, Huang personal-conduct coverage, market-size press releases, and unverified model launches.
